$comment: Which control-plane operations may be published on docs.thatch.cloud.
scripts/filter-openapi.mjs reads this, and refuses to run if the spec it is
given contains an operationId listed in neither array. That is deliberate:
a new endpoint added upstream cannot reach a public website just because
nobody remembered to classify it. If in doubt, it is internal.
Both lists are empty because the contract this is meant to filter does not
exist yet. The customer-facing surface is the OpenAI-compatible serving API
gated by a thatch_sk_ API key). The only artifact the control plane emits
today is portal.openapi.json, which is the Portal SPA's session-token
contract for tenant deployments — a different surface and a different
audience. Fill these in once a serving-surface artifact is emitted.
'servers' overrides the servers block in the source document: the portal
contract declares a same-origin proxy URL, which is meaningless to someone
reading these docs and calling the API from their own machine.
